sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, and risk rises steeply as utilization climbs, especially above about 60% of the credit limit.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises with it, with the largest jump between zero and one past delinquency.
Higher income is associated with lower predicted risk, though its effect is moderate to weak.
A longer credit history is associated with lower predicted risk, with a moderate to weak effect.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies, so high utilization matters far more for applicants who have delinquencies.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, with risk somewhat higher above a ratio of about 0.44.
Age has a negligible effect, and the data do not settle whether the two application attributes matter at all.
